title: Signal Daily — AI
summary: AI collection returned 135 unique items, though some Reddit feeds failed. Five stories cover agent evaluation, Jev tooling, local models, memory and research review; summaries are limited to collected titles and descriptions.

stories.headline: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
stories.dek: Research, commentary and tooling address evaluation of language-model agents.
tldr: An arXiv paper is titled “LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces.”
A separate Hacker News article explains the LLM-as-a-Judge approach.
A GitHub project describes agent evaluations and guardrails in one request.

body.text: The arXiv title raises trace integrity; separate items cover LLM-as-a-Judge and a project for agent evaluations and guardrails. The listings do not establish a shared benchmark or comparison.

stories.whyItMatters: The items show evaluation and trace integrity as distinct questions in agent development.
stories.editorNote: Metadata-only synthesis; no paper results or software were independently examined.

cluster.title: What is LLM-as-a-Judge, and How It Works?
openlayer-ai/jevals: Agent evals and guardrails as Jev decisions: one request per trace, a fraction of a cent, fast enough for the agent loop. Runs locally with Kev or Laya.

stories.headline: Running local LLMs on your Mac: what fits, what's free, and what's overkill
stories.dek: Today’s items span local inference, open-weight models and a video about falling model costs.
tldr: A Hacker News link asks which local language models fit on a Mac.
A GitHub listing describes Hemmingway-1 as a 27B model with open weights and non-commercial terms.
A YouTube title frames GLM 5.3 as powerful AI becoming almost free.

body.text: The primary link asks what fits on a Mac and what is free or excessive. Separate listings describe Hemmingway-1 as a 27B open-weight model and GLM 5.3 as becoming almost free; the records do not establish that either runs locally.

stories.whyItMatters: The items raise questions about hardware, licensing and price, but metadata supports no performance comparison.
stories.editorNote: Details follow titles and descriptions only; model terms and cost were not independently checked.
